$comment: Field reference for topics/backlog.json — the standing pool of meetup topics. Read this next to topics/backlog.json. Scoring weights live in config/topics.json; `npm run topics` scores and ranks, it never edits your judgement.

updated.description: YYYY-MM-DD the backlog was last curated by a human.

speakers.description: The standing speaker pipeline, independent of any one topic. A person here is someone who has actually been approached or has volunteered — never a wish.

source.description: Where this came from: a comment, a 接龙 reply, an intro. Same rule as numbers — no ghost speakers.

topic.description: The topic as you would say it out loud to a speaker, not a poster title.

angle.description: The specific cut: what the audience walks away able to do.

format.description: Drives the organising-cost points in config/topics.json.

evidence.description: REQUIRED. Each entry is '<event-slug>:<path-into-results>', e.g. '2026-09-17-agent-security-ke-he:qa_questions[3].q'. `npm run topics` resolves every one of them: A = resolves and the block carries checked+source, B = resolves without provenance metadata, D = does not resolve. A candidate with no A/B evidence is listed but never ranked.

audience_fit.description: How well it fits the audience that actually turns up (see the audience table the shortlist prints). 0 unless audience_fit_why says why.

channel_pull.description: Will the channels that actually pull people carry it? Needs a reason.

speaker.description: The real bottleneck. status: confirmed > asked > shortlist > idea > none.

status.description: candidate = in the running (the only status that gets ranked). scheduled/done link to `event`. dropped needs `dropped_why`.

event.description: Slug of the event that used this topic, once scheduled or done — this is what closes the loop back to results.

outcome.description: One line on how it went once done, pointing at the event's results (e.g. '22 RSVP / 692 领英展示, see 2026-09-17…:meetup.rsvps').

origin.description: Where the candidate came from, e.g. '2026-09-17-…:next_topics[0]' when harvested from a 复盘.
